key_insight: TrialOutlook used public evidence and GPT-5 to predict whether clinical trials would meet their primary endpoints, rather than discover cancer drugs.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support clinical research prioritization, but it does not establish treatment efficacy or guide individual patient care.
method: TrialDossier assembles standardized dossiers from publicly available evidence.
TrialOutlook uses GPT-5 to estimate each trial’s probability of meeting its prespecified primary endpoint.
Archived evidence and fixed forecasts are linked to subsequently adjudicated outcomes.
evidence_signal: Among 69 adjudicated outcomes from 694 ongoing trials, AUROC was 0.819 (95% CI, 0.708–0.914) and average precision was 0.860; 27 of 29 failures were identified, while 17 of 40 successes were incorrectly classified as failures.
watch_item: Only 69 outcomes were adjudicated, so performance needs confirmation as more results emerge; the abstract does not establish cancer-specific performance.
paper_title: Prospective prediction of clinical trial outcomes from public evidence
